title: "Conjura"
subtitle: "An open archive of unresolved conjectures in cryptography"
page-layout: full
---

Conjura collects **unresolved conjectures in cryptography**, precise write-ups that don't necessarily resolve a conjecture (clarifications of existing ideas, or corrections to gaps in existing papers), and the **prompts and tooling** used to work on them with AI assistance.

## Statement of Purpose

Progress in cryptography can be slow, and not only for mathematical reasons — uncoordinated effort and opaque tooling slow it down too. Conjura exists to make AI-assisted research on open problems public, so that work compounds instead of colliding: to advance the field faster by pointing available compute at conjectures collaboratively rather than in isolated silos, and to avoid collisions and repeated work by keeping a public record of what's been tried, resolved, or is still stuck. It is also an attempt to keep AI use transparent, publishing the prompts, tools, and sessions behind a result alongside it; to cut the slop, favoring precise, minimal write-ups over padded ones; and to add rigour through formal artifacts and machine-checked proofs where they're feasible. Beyond the conjectures themselves, we hope to produce better expository material — clear, informal explanations of results, not just formal statements — and to feed back to the AI community a record of how these tools actually perform against hard, unresolved problems. And, of course, to have some fun along the way.

## Explore

- [**Open Problems**](open-problems/index.qmd) — conjectures organized by topic, each with its current status, source material, and research session history.
- [**Papers**](papers/index.qmd) — write-ups that clarify or correct existing results without necessarily resolving a conjecture.
- [**Prompts**](prompts/index.qmd) — reusable prompts and skills for automating research in theoretical cryptography.
- [**Blog**](blog/index.qmd) — informal explanations, and eventually podcasts and videos, for resolved conjectures.

## Contributing

This site is built from plain files in its [GitHub repository](https://github.com/crypto-conjura/crypto-conjura.github.io). To submit a new conjecture, paper, or prompt, open a pull request; to flag a gap in a proof or discuss a conjecture, open an issue.
